Venugopal, seeking Mr. Kumar’s resignation and arrest for alleged electoral malpractice. Civil society groups and other organisations held parallel protests in Delhi and several States. Congress workers took to the streets across the country, with protests in several places being stopped by the police. Water cannons were used against demonstrators in Patna, Lucknow, and Punjab, while protesters were detained in Assam, Jammu, Odisha, Manipur, and other States. In Manipur’s capital, Imphal, the police fired a few tear-gas shells to disperse the protesters. In Keralam’s Malappuram, Mr. Venugopal said the protests would continue until the CEC stepped down. Targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, the Congress leader alleged that they were using Mr. Kumar to overcome public opposition to the government through “artificial manipulation”. The Congress accused the Election Commission of an “unprecedented attack” on voter equality, alleging that a specific ‘Mark VIP’ feature had been created in the BLO application. CEC Kumar cancelled two scheduled meetings in Uttar Pradesh. Poll body sources said these were not linked to the protests and were routine decisions. At Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, the campaign drew participation from civil society activists and organisations. The All India Students’ Association (AISA), along with civil society members, organised a protest demanding the arrest of Mr. Kumar. CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, AISA president Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav, lawyer Prashant Bhushan, RJD MP Manoj Jha, activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Nandita Narain were among those who participated. Several protesters, including Mr. Bhattacharya and Mr. Yadav, were detained by the Delhi Police. Delhi Congress chief Devender Yadav, who had organised a march from the Delhi Congress office to Nirvachan Sadan, the EC’s headquarters, was also detained by the police. Another protest was called by the Students’ Federation of India outside Nirvachan Sadan. The Indian Youth Congress separately staged a protest in Delhi. New Delhi Deputy Commissioner of Police Sachin Sharma said protesters were detained as no permission had been sought or granted to hold the protest at these venues. In Patna, the Bihar Congress marched towards the EC office but was stopped by the police using water cannons. Similar protests were reported in Lucknow, where Congress workers led by State president Ajay Rai clashed with the police after being stopped. In Assam, State Congress president Gaurav Gogoi and other leaders were detained when they attempted to march towards the Chief Electoral Officer’s office. In Jammu, Congress MP and AICC general secretary Syed Naseer Hussain led the protest, with several senior party leaders participating in the demonstration.
